problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Online convex optimization with an arbitrary sequence of differentiable losses f_t, each convex on the same nonempty compact convex set K. No strong convexity or Lipschitz-gradient assumption.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At round t, choose x_t in K before receiving exactly ∇f_t(x_t). The reply depends on history only through its length and is independent of the oracle seed. Execution makes exactly T gradient calls, with no additional initialization calls. Public information is d, K, x0, D, G, T; the loss sequence is hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: K is a subset of Euclidean R^d, with d a natural number, using the Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Known positive bounds D and G satisfy diam(K) ≤ D and ‖∇f_t(x)‖ ≤ G for every t and x in K. The positive integer horizon T is known. Losses need not obey any distributional or temporal regularity assumption.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: The regret inequality must hold for every combined algorithm/oracle seed ω and every comparator u, not merely in expectation or almost surely.

accuracy.details: Static cumulative regret: for every u in K, ∑_{t=0}^{T−1}[f_t(x_t)−f_t(u)] ≤ DG√T. Equivalently, average regret is at most DG/√T. Accuracy concerns the entire query trace; the terminal output is Unit.

descriptionHtml:
Online Convex Optimization

We consider online convex optimization on a nonempty compact convex set K⊆Rd, where d≥0 is an integer. The set has diameter at most D>0, and a point x0∈K is given. Each loss ft:Rd→R is convex on K and differentiable at every point of K, with gradient norm at most G>0. At round t, the oracle returns ∇ft(xt) at the chosen point xt∈K. Over T≥1 rounds, the goal is ∑t=0T−1[ft(xt)−ft(u)]≤B for every u∈K and every realization of algorithm randomness, where B∈R is the target regret bound.

The comparison is with the best fixed decision in hindsight, whose cumulative loss is minu∈K∑t=0T−1ft(u). Throughout, ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives d, K, x0, D, G, and the integer horizon T; the loss sequence is accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set). The set K is compact and convex, contains the given point x0, and satisfies ∥x−y∥≤D,x,y∈K.

Assumption 2 (Convex losses and bounded gradients). For every integer t≥0, the function ft is differentiable in the ambient space at every x∈K. For every x,y∈K and λ∈[0,1], ft((1−λ)x+λy)≤(1−λ)ft(x)+λft(y),∥∇ft(x)∥≤G.

At each round t=0,…,T−1, the algorithm chooses xt∈K using its randomness and previous oracle replies. The oracle returns ∇ft(xt) at xt. Thus there are exactly T gradient queries, one for each successive loss. The given point x0 is available to the algorithm; its first decision x0 is chosen by the algorithm.

The required performance concerns the decisions themselves. For a target bound B, which may depend on d,K,x0,D,G, and T, they must satisfy ∑t=0T−1ft(xt)−∑t=0T−1ft(u)≤B,for every u∈K, for every realization of the algorithm’s randomness and every loss sequence satisfying the assumptions.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Martin Zinkevich. Online Convex Programming and Generalized Infinitesimal Gradient Ascent. 2003 (ICML). Complexity: O(T) exact-gradient oracle calls, one per round, for deterministic regret O(DGT) using Greedy Projection; its proved bound is D2/(2ηT)+(G2/2)∑t=1Tηt, giving DGT with ηt=D/(GT). Equivalently, O(1+D2G2/ε2) calls suffice for average regret at most ε>0.
theorems.formulaHtml: D⋅G⋅T

import LongTails.TemplateOnline
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Topology.Compactness.Compact

namespace LongTails.Setups.OnlineConvexBoundedGradient

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
  x0 : K
  D : ℝ
  G : ℝ

structure Public extends Params where
  T : Horizon

abbrev spec : OnlineSetup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d) → ℝ
  Query p := p.K
  Reply p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Output _ := Unit
  publicInput p T := { toParams := p, T := T }
  valid p T := Convex ℝ p.K ∧ IsCompact p.K ∧ 0 < T ∧ 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.G ∧
    ∀ x ∈ p.K, ∀ y ∈ p.K, ‖x - y‖ ≤ p.D
  admissible p _ losses oracle :=
    (∀ t, ConvexOn ℝ p.K (losses t) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ p.K, HasGradientAt (losses t) (gradient (losses t) x) x ∧
        ‖gradient (losses t) x‖ ≤ p.G) ∧
    ∀ history query seed,
      oracle.answer history query seed = gradient (losses history.length) query.2
  successful p T losses result _ bound :=
    ∀ ω, let trace := (result ω).2
      ∀ u : p.K,
        (trace.zipIdx.map fun xt => losses xt.2 xt.1.1.2).sum -
          ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, losses t u.val ≤ bound

end LongTails.Setups.OnlineConvexBoundedGradient
